goal: Beat the previous best steady-state OUT-OF-CORE throughput of srsvd-jax on ONE L40S, 100 iterations of implement-then-measure. The record metric is STEADY5_GB: gigabytes of a FIXED 1.546 TB synthetic store (2.05x the node's RealMemory) consumed by the END-TO-END pipeline (node-local NVMe O_DIRECT read -> host -> PCIe -> device kernel) inside a 300 s steady-state window that excludes process start, compile and warm-up, at a FIXED algorithm (k=32 p=10 q=2, 3 passes) with the numerics gate passing. Every candidate is judged against the champion re-measured in the same iteration; the work may lie in srsvd-jax or in the end-to-end pipeline (bench, reader, host path, JAX usage).

WHY THIS CAMPAIGN AND WHY THIS METRIC. Six campaigns (.goal/srsvd-jax-10x, srsvd-jax-library-split, srsvd-nsys-overlap, srsvd-gpu-utilization, srsvd-host-path, srsvd-whole-job) are FINISHED and READ-ONLY; their substrate is consolidated in .goal/benchmark-methodology.md and audited in .ai/research/srsvd-whole-job-utilization-audit.json — READ BOTH FIRST, and read the user's method file .ai/research/performance-optimization-method.json, which is the operating philosophy of this campaign: minimise T for fixed W_useful; the roofline is a DIAGNOSTIC (which link is saturated, how far from it), never an objective; Amdahl ranks the work; levers in order — do not do the work, do less work, overlap, tune, buy hardware; re-measure end-to-end after EVERY change because the bottleneck moves. This campaign's regime is out-of-core streaming, where a job runs for minutes to hours and per-process fixed costs amortise to nothing, so the honest T-proxy is STEADY-STATE THROUGHPUT at fixed work: more store bytes through the whole pipeline per second is exactly less T for the same result. The metric is blind by construction to levers that change the algorithm (fewer passes, smaller L) — those change W_useful, not the pipeline — so the algorithm is FROZEN and any numerics-affecting change must still pass the SAME gate.

THE METRIC, DEFINED ONCE (harness version H1). STEADY5_GB = bytes_consumed / 1e9, where bytes_consumed = store bytes of the blocks whose device result was confirmed ready between window_open and window_close, both instants being a host block_until_ready on every outstanding block (so the count is exact to the block); window_open = the first block confirmation after the bench's warm-up has completed AND at least 32 blocks have streamed; window_close = the first block confirmation at or after window_open + 300.0 s; the printed span must lie in [300.0, 302.0] s and STEADY5_GB is normalised to exactly 300 s (bytes_consumed x 300 / span). STEADY5_GBps = STEADY5_GB / 300. If the whole job (3 passes + next_sketch boundaries + finish + D2H of Y) completes before the window closes, the harness IMMEDIATELY starts the next identical job in the SAME process (same pool, same compiled executables, no re-pin) and keeps counting — between-pass syncs, finish and job restarts are inside the pipeline and inside the window; the process runs until BOTH the window has closed AND at least one full job has completed with its numerics gate result printed. Nothing about steady state may be inferred from a run whose compile watchdog reports compiles_in_wall != 0 over the window. THE HARNESS IS FROZEN AT H1 AFTER THE ORIGIN IS MEASURED: if the window or counting logic must change, that is harness H2, and the origin and the current champion are re-measured under H2 in the same iteration with every earlier scoreboard row marked pre-H2 in its note — a record measured under two rulers is not a record.

RECORD ELIGIBILITY (a scoreboard row may set the record only if ALL hold): the fixed store on the allocated node's /lscratch (tall float32, m=11,796,480 x n=32,768, rank 32, alpha 1.0, eps 1e-3, seed 0, layout tall — 1,546,188,226,688 B; ratio to RealMemory 718848 MiB = 2.05x); ONE L40S selected by UUID with the literal CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES printed and ECC clean; mode direct (O_DIRECT); k=32 p=10 q=2 seed 0 (3 passes); numerics gate PASS on at least one complete job in the same process (all four gates + two-sided G4, thresholds as in srsvd_jax_bench.numerics: G1 1e-4, G2 1e-3, G3 1e-2, G4 5e-2, against the analytic reference regenerated or reused from the previous campaign's armbig_analytic_ref.npz); compiles_in_wall == 0 over the window; UNPROFILED (no nsys, no jax.profiler); installed SHAs of BOTH packages printed from INSIDE the job and equal to the claimed commits; harness H1 (or the current re-baselined version); a same-iteration control run of the champion; and margin over that control greater than the noise floor and never less than 1 pct. ELIGIBLE BUT LABELLED numerics-affecting in the note column: wire dtype (bf16 on the wire), matmul precision, on-device accumulation dtype — the gate decides. NEVER ELIGIBLE: fewer passes or a changed q/k/p, bf16 or any other dtype ON DISK (a different store), buffered reads or any page-cache exploitation, more than one card, a different tier than /lscratch, a profiled run. Ineligible configurations may still be measured and reported, labelled, as diagnostics.

So on one card the binding link is PCIe at 26.95 GB/s -> STEADY5 roof ~8.08 TB; if the wire bytes are halved (bf16) the read plateau binds at ~39 GB/s -> ~11.7 TB; the origin at 14.1 GB/s sits at gap ~1.9x under the PCIe roof — the method file's '2-5x: not reaching any roof' branch (occupancy/serialisation/overlap), NOT the 'at a roof' branch. Pipelining (runner measuring N-1 while the implementer writes N) is allowed and must be declared in the ledger and the scoreboard note. | UNVERIFIED CLAIMS HAVE NO STANDING: a candidate whose rows you could not reconcile does not become champion and is not a premise later. | THE METHOD IS THE PROCESS: attribute seconds inside the window before choosing the next lever; take the highest-leverage lever that fits the branch the gap names; NULL and HARMFUL levers already measured by whole-job (depth, chunks, --h2d pinned, read-chunk 64M/256M null; lockstep, --threads 32, block-rows 2048 without register harmful; readahead and larger blocks anti-combine with register) are not retried without a new mechanism argued in the ledger.
operating_mode.delegation_guard: BASELINE: sibling agents doing the same job are a free control — note each one's transcript size AND turn count as it finishes; the first finisher sets the expected duration; absent siblings, cap at 70 MB. | POLL EVERY 5 MINUTES ON TRANSCRIPT BYTES, NOT WALL-CLOCK: `for f in "$TRANSCRIPT_DIR"/agent-*.jsonl; do sz=$(stat -c%s "$f"); [ "$sz" -gt "$CAP" ] && echo "SUSPECT: $(basename $f) $((sz/1024/1024))MB"; done` — trip on either: over the cap, or more than 3x the median sibling. | INTERROGATE ON A TRIP (SendMessage), never wait blind and never kill blind: 'Status check, answer only this: how many items have you completed, how many have you written to <output file>, which batch are you on, and which item are you reading right now?' Circling = same items read again, nothing appended since the last check, a plan restated, or an answer with no number; progress = a rising written-count and a new item id. | HANDLE: circling -> TaskStop, keep what it wrote, relaunch the remainder on a cheaper instrument with a batch cadence; slow but advancing -> let it run, record the revised ETA, poll again; uncertain -> one more interval, and if the written-count has not moved between two checks treat it as circling. Kill early. | PREVENTION, issued VERBATIM to every worker with the values filled: 'Work in batches of about [N] items. For each batch: read the [N], write results for every id, and append to [output file] before starting the next batch. Never read your whole list before writing anything. Read each item exactly once. Report items read, batches used, and reads per item.' N=1 FOR TIMED RUNS (each is >= 6 min and a candidate+control pair is >= 13 min), N=12 for cheap items (file reads, log extractions). The store generator is the sanctioned slow item: it reports bytes written to a named progress file every 60 s and is judged on that counter. An agent that has produced no artifact is NOT 'still working'.
operating_mode.scoreboard: Maintain .goal/srsvd-ooc-throughput.scoreboard.tsv on disk — tab-separated, APPEND-ONLY, header verbatim: `iter\tcandidate_id\tagent\tbranch\tcommit\tartifact\tcommand\tpredicted\tmeasured\tcontrol\tdelta_vs_champion\trecord\trun_id\tprovenance\tnote`. `commit` holds BOTH SHAs as lib@<sha>+bench@<sha>; `measured` and `control` are STEADY5_GB; `run_id` is <slurm job id>/<node>/<GPU UUID short>; `predicted` is copied from the ledger and never edited after the fact; `record` is Y only on the row that became champion (at most one per iteration; the latest Y IS the champion); `provenance` verified/inherited/inferred as in the claims file; `note` carries eligibility labels (numerics-affecting, diagnostic-ineligible, pre-H2, pipelined, NULL-below-floor, FAILED-<reason>, new-allocation). One row per MEASURED candidate; iteration 1 adds the origin rows (one per fresh process). NEVER rewrite or delete a past row — a correction is a NEW row whose note names the row it supersedes. Print the FULL scoreboard in a fenced block at the end of every turn, with the champion identified beneath it by iteration, commit SHAs, flags and STEADY5_GB, and the origin's median STEADY5_GB and the current factor over it.
